svg.title: Layering the Stack From Cheapest Money to Risk Capital
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-capital-stack-roadmap; chapter number: 12; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Layering the Stack From Cheapest Money to Risk Capital; subtitle: Senior debt, bridge, tax credits, and litigation funding; caption: Cheapest senior money goes in first; expensive risk capital is rented only where the gap demands it.; assumptions note: The week-by-week sequence is an organizing order, not a timeline any speaker prescribed; every rate, price and ratio is as stated by the cited source.; note: Sources are Break Into CRE, Jeremiah Boucher of Patriot Holdings, Jason Prince via Tax Alpha Insider, and Statera Capital via The National Law Review.; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Map the capital stack; deliverable: Senior debt at 50-65% of cost, with mezzanine and preferred equity priced at 15-20% all-in (Break Into CRE); gate: Senior capacity sized before any risk capital is sought; week: Week 2; title: Price the bridge loan; deliverable: 7-12% rate, 65-80% LTV, 1% up to 3-4% origination, close in 5-60 days, with capex funding and a 12-month interest reserve requested; gate: Exit mapped and default provisions redlined by an attorney; week: Week 3; title: Place transferable tax credits; deliverable: About 85 cents on the dollar, about 92 cents with insurance, parent guarantees and Big-4 memos, about 80 cents for risk-takers; gate: Prevailing wage and apprenticeship records verified before paying above the 80-cent tier; week: Week 4; title: Approach litigation funders; deliverable: Targeted pitch aiming at 2-4x returns, with realistic case value near 10x the commitment; gate: NDA, budget, timeline and case outline in hand; only 3-5% of cases are accepted
